description: Baseline: buy and hold SPX at 100% weight, no tuning; execution is next-open to following-open with 0.05% buy/sell costs.
Cash reference: verify zero-return zero-drawdown feasible anchor; no tuning.

Long-horizon trend: hold above 200-session SMA to avoid sustained declines. Method inspiration Faber 2013-02-01 https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=962461 ; adapt monthly trend concept to daily signals.
Medium-horizon trend: SMA50 can exit declines earlier, with expected whipsaw cost relative to slow trend; distinct horizon hypothesis.
Trend confirmation: require price above SMA200 and SMA50 above SMA200; attempt to reduce false recoveries.
Time-series momentum: positive 126-session trailing return signals persistence; method source AQR 2012-05-01 https://www.aqr.com/Insights/Research/Journal-Article/Time-Series-Momentum .
Multi-horizon momentum: average positive signs over 21/63/126/251 sessions for graded risk allocation rather than a single binary trend.

Volatility-managed exposure: cap 20-day realized annual volatility near 15%, no leverage. Source Moreira/Muir April 2016 https://www.nber.org/papers/w22208 ; adapt mechanism to constrained equity/cash exposure.
Combine slow trend with volatility scaling: expect large downside reduction at possible cost to recovery participation; Faber 2013 and Moreira/Muir 2016 methods.
Conditional short-term reversal: in a positive SMA200 regime buy RSI2 below 10, exit on RSI2 above 60 or regime break; state uses only earlier observations.
Bollinger reversal: buy below 20-session lower two-sigma band and exit at moving average; test transitory overshoot hypothesis without calendar assumptions.
Price breakout with hysteresis: enter above prior 55-session close maximum, exit below prior 20-session minimum, avoiding repeated symmetric threshold switching.
Regime blend: fully hold positive slow trend; otherwise use half-weight after a short-term oversold signal to participate in rebounds without full bearish-regime exposure.

Training-only ridge forecast: 13 causal OHLC/trend/reversal/volatility features; choose ridge penalty by prediction MSE on chronological last 30% of training, purge 2 boundary labels; refit on all training. Invest when predicted next-open return > 0. No validation labels or calendar features.

Forecast hysteresis: same training-only ridge procedure as prior candidate, but require predicted return > 5bp to enter and < -5bp to exit, relating turnover control to one-way cost. Hypothesis: small noisy sign changes should not cause full round trips.

Forecast risk allocation: same training-only ridge estimates, convert conditional expected return into clipped weight mu/(2*20-day variance); no leverage. Hypothesis: position sizing can use forecast magnitude without binary turnover.

Nonlinear conditional returns: 24 bootstrap trees, fixed depth 3, random feature subsets and 50-observation shrinkage to training mean; all fitting on training labels. Source Gu/Kelly/Xiu, RFS May 2020, https://doi.org/10.1093/rfs/hhaa009 ; adapt tree interaction concept, not their empirical strategies. Positive forecast invests.

Nonlinear forecast with cost hysteresis: same fixed training-only forest, 5bp positive/negative thresholds to enter/exit. Ridge comparison suggested cost-aware persistence is preferable to rapid forecast sign trading.

Shrunk regime table: estimate next-open returns separately by slow trend, normalized 5-day reversal and training-tercile volatility; 80 pseudo-observations of global mean per cell, cost hysteresis. Tests whether simple interactions outperform linear forecasting without deep model complexity.

Acute volatility shock control: exit only on 5/60-day volatility ratio above 2 plus price below SMA20, reenter after SMA10 recovery or ratio below 1.4. Hypothesis: rapid risk escalation deserves faster response than persistent slow-trend exclusion; all inputs causal.

Combine learned return forecast with acute-risk control: retain the ridge cost-hysteresis entry decision, but require the independently promising 5/60 volatility-shock gate. Tests complementary prediction and tail-risk signals, not date-specific rules.

Conservative recovery after volatility shock: same causal risk trigger as current champion, but reenter only when price recovers above SMA10. Tests whether volatility normalization alone can produce premature reentry during ongoing price weakness.

Downside-only risk acceleration: replace symmetric volatility shock by ratio of 5-day versus 60-day downside RMS, retaining original price confirmation/reentry. Positive-return volatility should not itself trigger protection.

Training-calibrated shock threshold: estimate 95th-percentile 5/60 volatility ratio solely from training OHLC history, with 70th-percentile normalization reentry. Tests transferable distribution-based cutoffs rather than arbitrary validation tuning.

Combine successful downside-risk and training calibration: use 5/60 negative-return RMS ratio with training-only 95th/70th percentiles; otherwise unchanged price confirmation and reentry. Tests whether positive volatility causes avoidable false exits.

OHLC risk acceleration: ratio of 3-day mean true range to 60-day median true range, normalized by prior close; train-only 95/70 percentile calibration. Captures gaps and intraday stress invisible in close-return dispersion; robust denominator resists isolated spikes.

EWMA risk acceleration: ratio of return RMS using 5-session versus 30-session half-lives, train-only percentile calibration; avoid abrupt rolling-window expiration in the promising volatility-shock model.
Downside magnitude breadth: average absolute negative returns over 5 versus 60 sessions, training percentile calibration. Tests persistent smaller losses rather than a few squared-return extremes.

Normalize reentry only in moderate absolute volatility: preserve calibrated shock exit, but ratio recovery needs 20-day volatility below its training 80th percentile unless price recovers SMA10. Addresses risk staying elevated after its growth rate slows.

Two-stage risk recovery: use champion trigger, restore half exposure on volatility normalization and full exposure only on SMA10 recovery. Tests whether gradual reentry improves growth by reducing early recovery whipsaws.

Earlier risk confirmation: replace price-below-SMA20 with a negative one-session close return, preserving training-calibrated volatility shock thresholds. Tests the delay caused by waiting for slow price confirmation.

Fast low-break confirmation: use close below prior three closes to distinguish directional downside stress from non-directional volatility, instead of SMA20 confirmation. Recovery unchanged; no future or calendar information.

Trend-recovery gate through the full stress event: calibrated shock detection with default SMA20 confirmation, but no full reinvestment while ratio remains above the exit percentile even after SMA10 rebound. Tests false reentry during unresolved stress.

Slow-drawdown complementary protection: add a training-calibrated 95th percentile normalized 63-day drawdown to the shock gate, requiring price below SMA50. Relative volatility may normalize during sustained declines; normalized drawdown can detect this distinct regime.

Price-led recovery: retain trained volatility shock exit and three-close downside confirmation; reenter on close above prior three closes or normalized volatility. Hypothesis: local upward breakout restores exposure earlier without calendar rules.

Confirmed recovery: retain trained shock exit; replace SMA reentry with two consecutive positive close returns or volatility normalization. Hypothesis: sequential price recovery distinguishes bounce from continued stress.

Train-only expanding-window selection: nine prespecified risk-tail/recovery-scale combinations, thresholds calibrated on past fold only, two boundary rows purged, select mean net log growth across two later training folds with 50% DD constraint; refit thresholds on all training. No validation parameter fitting.

Robust train-only expanding-window selection: same nine prespecified configurations and purged training folds; select worst-fold net log growth to test stability of parameter choice before fixed validation evaluation.

CUSUM directional shift detector: standardized 20-session cumulative negative returns with 0.5 drift allowance and threshold 5, volatility scale from preceding 60 returns; SMA10 recovery. Source NIST Engineering Statistics Handbook, 2012 archive (web page undated), https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/pmc/section3/pmc323.htm . Hypothesis: persistent small losses can identify regime change before volatility jumps.

Complementary CUSUM and volatility-shock gate: add standardized cumulative-loss alarm (NIST 2012 handbook source https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/pmc/section3/pmc323.htm) to trained shock gate; recover on SMA10 or both normalized shock and cumulative stress. Tests slow persistent losses plus abrupt shocks.

OHLC range-energy shock: replace close-return dispersion with square-root ratio of mean squared log(high/low) over 5 vs 60 sessions. Same train-only 95/70 calibration, low-break exit and SMA10 recovery. Hypothesis: intraday range expansion can detect stress despite close-to-close cancellation; raw observed OHLC only.

Instantaneous downside outlier: replace 5/60 volatility acceleration with largest standardized negative return in recent three sessions, each normalized against its preceding 60 returns. Train-only 95/70 calibration, low-break confirmation and SMA10 recovery. Hypothesis: single large jumps may be obscured by symmetric sample dispersion.

Rolling exponential expert mixture: full exposure, cash, 20/100-day trend and 5-day reversal, weighted by last 60 fully observed close-to-close net proxy returns with temperature 10. Actual evaluation remains next-open. Source Arora/Hazan/Kale 2012 https://mirror.theoryofcomputing.org/articles/v008a006/ . Hypothesis: causal expert adaptation can handle changing persistence vs reversal; no forward labels used.

Expert mixture within acute-risk gate: combine causal exponential weighting of five prespecified experts with current training-calibrated volatility-shock protection. Source Arora/Hazan/Kale 2012 https://mirror.theoryofcomputing.org/articles/v008a006/ . Tests complementary continuous exposure adaptation; only fully observed trailing close returns score experts.

Training-only 5-session mean log-return ridge forecast: use contiguous training forward returns, chronological ridge penalty CV with 6-row purge, full refit; hysteresis round-trip cost divided by horizon. Hypothesis: multi-session labels improve signal/noise relative to one-session prediction; no validation fitting.

Combine 5-session training-only log-return forecast with calibrated 5/60 volatility-shock gate. Same purged training CV and horizon-scaled cost hysteresis as paired ablation; tests complementary expected return and acute risk protection.

Training-only 20-session mean log-return ridge forecast: use contiguous training forward returns, chronological ridge penalty CV with 21-row purge, full refit; hysteresis round-trip cost divided by horizon. Hypothesis: multi-session labels improve signal/noise relative to one-session prediction; no validation fitting.

Combine 20-session training-only log-return forecast with calibrated 5/60 volatility-shock gate. Same purged training CV and horizon-scaled cost hysteresis as paired ablation; tests complementary expected return and acute risk protection.

Train-only downside classifier: regularized logistic probability of next five-session return below -3%, 14 causal OHLC/trend/volatility features; fixed optimization and training score 95/70 quantiles control risk hysteresis. Hypothesis: predicting rare loss events is more useful than predicting every return sign. No validation labels, no calendar features.

Learned downside classifier plus acute shock protection: pair five-session training-only logistic downside probability with current calibrated volatility gate. Tests learned nonlinear probability of loss as complementary protection; no refitting on validation.

Quarter-scale return forecast: extend training target to 60-session mean log return and purge 61 boundary rows for ridge CV; round-trip cost spread over 60 sessions. Same acute-risk gate. Hypothesis: slower persistence may be more predictable than monthly return; distinct horizon, not a fine grid.

Equal-weight weekly/monthly/quarterly forecast ensemble: 5/20/60-session mean log-return ridge models independently selected by purged chronological training CV; average daily-return forecasts before cost hysteresis and risk gate. Hypothesis: horizon diversification reduces dependence on a single label scale.

Monthly model with partial exposure during negative forecasts: retain half index weight when forecast turns negative, while acute volatility protection can still go fully to cash. Hypothesis: forecast sign is noisy and partial participation reduces missed recoveries without weakening shock exit.

Robust monthly ridge labels: clip training target tails at fitting-subset 2.5/97.5 percentiles, separately within each purged CV fit and final refit. Evaluation labels remain unchanged. Hypothesis: a few extreme training windows may dominate mean-square estimation and harm transferable forecasts.

Decision-focused training CV: choose monthly ridge penalty by chronological training-fold net portfolio growth under existing cost/risk rules rather than forecast MSE. Purge 21 rows, calibrate risk thresholds only on earlier fold; outer validation policy untouched. Hypothesis: prediction loss and invest/cash decisions need not select the same model.

Block-bagged monthly forecasts: twelve ridge models fitted to fixed-seed 40-session moving-block resamples of training feature-label pairs, ridge penalty selected by original purged training CV; average predictions with same gate. Hypothesis: block resampling reduces sensitivity to particular overlapping monthly targets while respecting training-only fitting.

Monthly forecast close-only ablation: retain normalized return/trend/volatility/drawdown inputs, remove four daily OHLC candle features. Same training CV and gate. Hypothesis: single-day intraday structure may add noise to a 20-session target.

Monthly forecast using technical indicators: replace feature set by fixed RSI2/14, MACD12/26/9 levels/histogram, Bollinger20 normalized position/width, monthly/six-month momentum and 5/60 volatility ratio. Frozen indicator library, all trailing observations; same purged training CV and gate. Tests smooth path information rather than single-bar structure.

Technical-indicator augmentation of monthly forecast: append fixed RSI2/14, normalized MACD and Bollinger20 location/width to existing 13 causal features. Same training-only penalty selection and risk gate. Paired with replacement ablation to distinguish complementary from redundant information.

State interaction features for monthly ridge: add reversal-times-trend and momentum-times-volatility interactions plus squared short reversal and drawdown. Coefficients fitted only on training, purged penalty CV retained. Hypothesis: linear forecast can miss differing reversal behavior across trend/risk states.

Overnight/intraday decomposition features: append trailing 5/20-session mean close/open and open/previous-close log returns normalized by daily volatility. Current and historical OHLC only, all observed by signal close. Hypothesis: persistent gap and session components contain different information for monthly returns.

Raw-scale monthly forecast ablation: use unnormalized log returns over 1/5/21/63/126 sessions, moving-average distance, drawdown and realized volatility. Same train scaling, purged ridge selection and risk gate. Hypothesis: volatility-normalizing every trend feature can remove economically relevant magnitude information.

Recency-weighted monthly ridge: exponentially weight training observations with 504-session half-life in centering, scaling, target mean and least squares, separately inside each purged CV fit. Same close-only features and fixed risk gate. Hypothesis: relationships drift, so recent training evidence should count more without discarding older observations.

Trailing-training-window monthly model: each training-model fit uses only its most recent 756 labeled samples; purge/CV and frozen outer protocol unchanged, risk calibration still uses all available training rows. Hypothesis: recent three-year relationships may transfer better than a decade average.

Equal blend of full-training and last-756-sample monthly ridge estimates: select shared regularization with purged chronological CV using blend predictions. Same gate. Hypothesis: preserve long-run evidence while adapting to recent relationships, reducing sensitivity to either training window alone.

Trend-conditioned monthly ridge mixture: fit separate above/below SMA200 regressions plus a pooled model; blend local and pooled forecasts equally, fallback if a group has fewer than 180 training samples. Selection via same purged training CV. Hypothesis: conditional trend regimes have distinct return relationships; no calendar rules.

Shrunk nearest-neighbor monthly forecast: 100 nearest training feature vectors in standardized close-only state space, 100 pseudo-observations of global training mean, 20-session training labels. Same cost hysteresis and risk gate. Hypothesis: local state analogues can capture nonlinear relationships missed by a single regression.

Shallow forest on monthly labels: reuse fixed 24-tree depth-3 architecture with 50-observation shrinkage, now fit training 20-session mean log returns using close-only features. Same gate. Method source Gu/Kelly/Xiu RFS May 2020 https://doi.org/10.1093/rfs/hhaa009 ; tests whether longer labels enable useful nonlinear interactions.

Method source Friedman, October 2001, https://doi.org/10.1214/aos/1013203451 . Monthly gradient-boosted stumps: additive residual fitting, learning rate .05, minimum leaves 60, leaf shrinkage 20; choose 20/60/120 stages by purged chronological training MSE and refit. Same risk gate. Hypothesis: additive nonlinear effects may be suppressed by bagged shallow forests.

Method source Friedman, October 2001, https://doi.org/10.1214/aos/1013203451 . Boosted monthly forecast without shock gate: paired ablation of independently learned nonlinear return timing, all training selection unchanged. Tests whether forecast alone learns useful stress behavior.

Method source Friedman, October 2001, https://doi.org/10.1214/aos/1013203451 . Robust gradient-boosted monthly forecast: clip pseudo-residuals at 1.5 fitting-subset target standard deviations (Huber-style gradients); training CV chooses number of stumps. Same shock gate. Hypothesis: limiting influence of extreme overlapping training windows can improve nonlinear generalization.

Method source Friedman, October 2001, https://doi.org/10.1214/aos/1013203451 . Weekly gradient-boosted forecast with shock gate: five-session average log-return target, six-row purge and horizon-scaled cost hysteresis, training CV selects stage count. Hypothesis: nonlinear short-horizon structure may survive where prior linear weekly model did not improve.

Method source Friedman, October 2001, https://doi.org/10.1214/aos/1013203451 . Linear forecast plus boosted residual corrections: initialize each training fit with fixed ridge .1, then train additive stumps on remaining error. Purged chronological training CV selects correction stage count. Same close-only features and shock gate. Hypothesis: preserve smooth extrapolation while correcting systematic nonlinear residuals.

Smooth monthly forecasts before position decisions: five-session-span EMA of successive causal forecast values, unchanged cost hysteresis and instantaneous shock gate. Hypothesis: overlapping monthly targets should not cause daily position reversals on forecast noise.

Two-observation forecast confirmation: require two consecutive forecasts beyond the entry/exit cost threshold before changing forecast position; keep acute-risk gate daily. Hypothesis: simple persistence confirmation reduces spurious forecast sign flips without imposing a fixed holding period.

Staggered-sleeve forecast allocation: equal average of last five binary forecast recommendations, padded initially by current recommendation, multiplied by daily acute-risk gate. Hypothesis: spreading discretionary changes across independent daily sleeves reduces timing sensitivity and turnover; no calendar schedule.

Continuous approximate log-growth allocation: interpret monthly forecast as daily log drift; combine with trailing 20-session return variance to set clipped weight 0.5+mu/variance, then apply acute-risk gate. Hypothesis: smooth exposure can use forecast magnitude instead of only its sign; strictly zero to one exposure.

Decision-focused joint training calibration: select ridge penalty and four prespecified cost-derived hysteresis widths (zero, round-trip/20, one round-trip, two round-trips) by purged chronological training net growth subject to 50% DD. Calibrate gate only on earlier fold, refit model on training; never select threshold using validation labels.

Volatility-standardized monthly training target: divide forward mean log return by signal-time trailing 20-day volatility before ridge fitting and purged CV; multiply forecast back into daily log-return units before fixed cost threshold. Same risk gate. Hypothesis: normalize heteroskedastic target scale rather than only input features.

Monthly residual-to-trend target: fit future daily log return minus currently observed 63-session average log drift, restore that baseline at inference. Same purged training selection and shock gate. Hypothesis: predicting departures from a causal trend baseline may be easier than predicting unconditional returns.

Downside-weighted monthly ridge: give negative monthly training outcomes double weight in fitted moments and least squares, with regularization still selected by unweighted purged training MSE. Outer reward unchanged. Hypothesis: a deliberate downside-sensitive forecast may avoid harmful optimistic estimates while retaining the acute-risk gate.

Nonoverlapping-phase monthly ensemble: train twenty ridge regressions, each sampling every twentieth labeled row at a different offset; average predictions. Each component has nonoverlapping 20-session targets. Same purged chronological training CV and acute-risk gate. Hypothesis: reduce repeated-window influence without selecting a calendar phase or discarding most observations overall.

Locally adaptive volatility-shock gate: derive 95/70 ratio percentiles from strictly earlier rolling windows within current 252-session history, excluding current return; monthly forecast unchanged. Hypothesis: risk acceleration distribution can drift beyond the frozen training distribution, while current shock should not set its own threshold.

Shrunk adaptive volatility gate: average local trailing-history 95/70 thresholds with full-training thresholds, retaining monthly forecast. Same strictly causal local windows as paired adaptive ablation. Hypothesis: pooling stable training estimates with limited recent history reduces noisy threshold drift.

Trend-conditioned risk calibration: estimate separate training-only 95/70 volatility-ratio thresholds above versus below SMA200, use currently observed regime to select them; keep pooled thresholds if fewer than 180 observations. Monthly forecast unchanged. Hypothesis: stress distributions differ between trend states.

Forecast-assisted recovery from shock: preserve original exit rule; additionally permit recovery when volatility has fallen below exit threshold, price turns up, and monthly forecast exceeds its training-fitted 90th percentile. Hypothesis: strong expected recovery can justify earlier participation once acute stress decays; threshold uses training only.

Source Rabiner, February 1989, https://www.cs.ubc.ca/~murphyk/Bayes/rabiner.pdf . Two-state Gaussian HMM: 25 training-only EM iterations on close log returns, filtered-training posterior estimates next-open log-return means with 50-sample prior shrinkage. At each signal forward-filter only current trailing 252 closes; 5bp forecast hysteresis. Hypothesis: persistent latent volatility states can guide invest/cash decisions; no validation smoothing.

Source Rabiner, February 1989, https://www.cs.ubc.ca/~murphyk/Bayes/rabiner.pdf . Two-state filtered-return model plus acute volatility gate: paired ablation combines HMM conditional return timing with established shock protection. All HMM parameters and conditional returns fitted on training only; inference strictly forward on observed history.

Source Rabiner, February 1989, https://www.cs.ubc.ca/~murphyk/Bayes/rabiner.pdf . Three-state Gaussian HMM with acute-risk gate: calm/intermediate/stress variance initialization, otherwise same fixed EM and training conditional-return estimation. Hypothesis: two states may conflate ordinary corrections and extreme volatility; inference uses no future states.

Source Rabiner, February 1989, https://www.cs.ubc.ca/~murphyk/Bayes/rabiner.pdf . HMM stress-probability gate with existing monthly ridge: replace relative-volatility alarm by posterior probability above .8 for training-fitted highest-variance state, retain low-break confirmation and recover below .5 or SMA10. Hypothesis: persistent probabilistic stress detection is more informative than a ratio threshold; forward filtering only.

Lasso monthly forecast: L1 coordinate descent with standardized target and inputs, regularization selected by purged chronological training MSE. Same nine close-only inputs and risk gate. Hypothesis: a sparse predictive subset can reduce redundant feature noise. Source Tibshirani 1996 https://doi.org/10.1111/j.2517-6161.1996.tb02080.x .

Elastic-net monthly forecast: equal L1/L2 mixture, standardized target, training-only regularization selection. Same forecast horizon and risk gate. Hypothesis: combine sparsity with stability when momentum features are correlated. Source Zou/Hastie 2005 https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1467-9868.2005.00503.x .

Principal-component monthly regression: fit feature covariance and leading orthogonal components on each training subset, select 2/4/9 components by purged chronological training MSE, fixed .1 coefficient damping. Same acute-risk gate. Hypothesis: compress correlated feature directions and discard weak directions rather than individual indicators.

Grouped-feature forecast ensemble: separately regress monthly targets on short-horizon returns, long-horizon trend, and volatility/drawdown features; average three predictions, choose shared regularization via purged training CV. Hypothesis: separate estimation reduces cross-group coefficient instability without hand-selecting one winning feature.

Exact intercept after feature clipping: recenter transformed training features and fit unpenalized intercept consistently with their actual mean; same +/-5 standardized clipping, ridge CV and shock gate. Hypothesis: clipping asymmetric tails shifts feature means, so target mean alone is not the fitted intercept. Includes training-only fitted-mean consistency assertion.

Smooth feature-tail compression: replace hard +/-5 truncation by asinh of standardized features, then recenter and fit exact intercept. Same training-only ridge selection and risk gate. Hypothesis: preserve ordering beyond observed extremes while limiting outlier magnitude continuously.

Unclipped linear extrapolation ablation: standardize features without truncation, exact centered intercept, same ridge CV and shock gate. Hypothesis: clipping out-of-training-range states may hide useful strength of the monthly linear signal; long-only bounded allocation remains enforced.

Robust feature location/scale: median and 1.4826 times median absolute deviation fitted within each training fold, +/-5 clipping followed by exact recentering/intercept. Same monthly ridge CV and risk gate. Hypothesis: typical-state scaling should be less influenced by extreme training episodes.

Three-fold expanding training CV: select monthly ridge penalty by average MSE across three successive later training blocks, purge 21 rows before and at end of each scored fold. Refit all training and retain original gate. Hypothesis: a single late training split may favor a regime-specific model.

Regime-balanced training CV: same three purged expanding folds, normalize each fold MSE by that fold target variance before selecting monthly ridge penalty. Refit all training, original risk gate. Hypothesis: high-volatility training folds should not dominate regularization selection solely through larger return scale.

Out-of-fold training bias correction: estimate average monthly forecast residual on the purged late training block and add that bias estimate to the final refit intercept. All labels restricted to training; same gate and transaction thresholds. Hypothesis: fitting bias on seen samples can miss persistent out-of-sample calibration error.

Training-error and leverage-aware forecast hysteresis: use late-training out-of-fold RMS error, effective sample count n/20 for overlapping monthly labels, and ridge feature leverage to widen thresholds for uncertain forecasts. Heuristic uncertainty scale, no claimed coverage; same gate and unlevered position bounds.

Price-path persistence features: append signed 20/60-session path efficiency, positive-return fraction, lag-one return autocorrelation, and age of 63-session high to close-only monthly ridge. Same purged training CV and shock gate. Hypothesis: paths with similar terminal momentum can differ in persistence and choppiness.

Trailing return-distribution features: append 60-session standardized skewness, excess kurtosis, downside squared-return share, and largest absolute-return share. Same monthly training procedure and shock gate. Hypothesis: concentrated downside tails provide information beyond symmetric volatility and total drawdown.

Aggregated candle-shape features: append five/twenty-session means of body-to-range, close location and upper-minus-lower wick balance; exclude single-day candle inputs. Same monthly ridge CV and shock gate. Hypothesis: persistent intraday buying/selling pressure may matter when isolated candle shape was noisy.

Trend-fit quality features: append trailing 20/60-session log-price linear slopes divided by daily return volatility and signed fit R-squared. Same close-only monthly regression, training CV and gate. Hypothesis: stable directional movement may be more predictive than equally sized erratic movement.

Method inspiration Moody/Saffell, July 2001, https://people.idsia.ch/~juergen/rnnaissance2003talks/MoodySaffellTNN01.pdf . Direct feedforward policy optimization: sigmoid long-only allocation from nine causal features, exact training net log-growth gradients including 5bp proportional costs, drift and liquidation. Select regularization and 100/300 steps by purged late-training net growth; no reward forecasting stage, no validation fitting.

Method inspiration Moody/Saffell, July 2001, https://people.idsia.ch/~juergen/rnnaissance2003talks/MoodySaffellTNN01.pdf . Direct allocation policy plus established acute-risk gate: paired ablation of training-optimized sigmoid weights with independent volatility protection. Same exact-cost training objective and chronological parameter selection; bounded unlevered exposure.

Method inspiration Moody/Saffell, July 2001, https://people.idsia.ch/~juergen/rnnaissance2003talks/MoodySaffellTNN01.pdf . Binary execution of directly learned policy: optimize smooth allocation surrogate on earlier training; late-training selection uses .6/.4 binary hysteresis and exact costs. Apply independent risk gate in final candidate. Hypothesis: sparse position changes can improve net growth relative to continuous small rebalances.

Method inspiration Moody/Saffell, July 2001, https://people.idsia.ch/~juergen/rnnaissance2003talks/MoodySaffellTNN01.pdf . Nonlinear-feature direct policy: add reversal/trend and momentum/volatility products to sigmoid allocation inputs; optimize net log growth and choose capacity only within training as paired linear policy. Same acute-risk gate. Hypothesis: return-maximizing interactions can differ from those selected by forecast MSE.

Method inspiration Moody/Saffell, July 2001, https://people.idsia.ch/~juergen/rnnaissance2003talks/MoodySaffellTNN01.pdf . Train-execution alignment for direct allocation: include the calibrated acute-risk gate in both net-growth gradients and chronological training selection, with each fold calibrating thresholds solely on its earlier training subset. Risk-off observations contribute no position gradient, but their exit/entry costs remain. Hypothesis: train the policy for the states where it will actually trade.

Method inspiration Moody/Saffell, July 2001, https://people.idsia.ch/~juergen/rnnaissance2003talks/MoodySaffellTNN01.pdf . Gated direct policy with binary execution: train smooth risk-gated allocation; select training regularization and stages using .6/.4 binary forecast hysteresis plus the same gate and exact costs. Hypothesis: aligning risk control and sparse execution during selection improves transfer.

Method inspiration Moody/Saffell, July 2001, https://people.idsia.ch/~juergen/rnnaissance2003talks/MoodySaffellTNN01.pdf . Interaction policy trained with risk gate: add reversal/trend and momentum/volatility interactions to direct return-maximizing allocation; include fixed-within-fit risk protection in training gradients and chronological selection. Tests nonlinear decisions specifically in risk-on periods.

Method source Kalman, March 1960, https://eceweb1.rutgers.edu/~gajic/pdffiles/519KalmanFiltering/kalman1960.pdf . Local linear state-space trend timing: forward-filter trailing 252 log closes with level/slope states, observation noise from currently observed 60-return variance. Select one of three slope process-noise scales on later training net growth, cost hysteresis; no retrospective smoothing. Hypothesis: latent trend estimates may reduce moving-average lag.

Method source Kalman, March 1960, https://eceweb1.rutgers.edu/~gajic/pdffiles/519KalmanFiltering/kalman1960.pdf . Kalman trend plus acute-risk gate: same local linear state model; training scale selection includes independently calibrated shock protection and costs. Hypothesis: smooth trend estimates and fast stress exits address different timescales.

Method source Kalman, March 1960, https://eceweb1.rutgers.edu/~gajic/pdffiles/519KalmanFiltering/kalman1960.pdf . State-space feature augmentation: append normalized local-linear slope, standardized final innovation and slope uncertainty from fixed .001 process-noise filter to monthly ridge. Training-only ridge selection, same shock gate. Hypothesis: filtered trend and unexpected price changes can complement raw momentum.

Direction-probability monthly forecast: regularized logistic model for positive 20-session return, combine probability with training-average positive and negative magnitudes to predict daily log drift. Select penalty by purged chronological training return MSE, same cost hysteresis and shock gate. Hypothesis: direction can be easier to learn than exact return magnitude.

Two-part monthly forecast: logistic direction probability plus separate ridge models of positive/negative magnitudes, constrained nonnegative. Shared penalty selected by purged training expected-return MSE. Same shock gate. Hypothesis: asymmetric up/down dynamics require separate magnitude relationships rather than one average-return regression.

Weekly direction-probability forecast: positive five-session target with separate empirical average gain/loss, six-row training purge and cost threshold scaled by horizon. Same risk gate. Hypothesis: short-horizon direction classification may improve where weekly direct-return regression was noisy.

Additive quadratic monthly regression: include linear and squared standardized close-only features, recenter/rescale expanded columns within every training fit, select ridge penalty by purged CV. Same gate. Hypothesis: feature-return relationships may curve without requiring complex interactions.

Additive Gaussian-basis monthly regression: linear inputs plus smooth radial features around standardized values -1,0,1 for each individual feature; train-only basis scaling and ridge CV, same gate. Hypothesis: bounded local nonlinear responses can model reversals more naturally than global polynomials.

Multivariate Gaussian-prototype monthly regression: choose up to sixteen diverse centers by training-feature farthest-point coverage, append smooth kernels with squared bandwidth equal to feature count to linear features. Fit and rescale only within training folds; same ridge CV and gate. Hypothesis: locally smooth state interactions can complement linear extrapolation.

Train-only simple-rule selection: two chronological late-training folds rank 11 fixed cash/trend/momentum/reversal/breakout experts by exact net log growth under 50% drawdown; choose one. No validation parameter tuning; each fold's shock thresholds calibrated only on purged preceding training although gate disabled.

Train-only simple-rule selection with volatility-shock gate: rank same 11 fixed experts by summed net growth on two chronological training folds, calibrate 95/70 shock thresholds on preceding purged training, select top one then freeze. Test whether explicit rule selection beats fitted monthly forecasts.

Training-selected equal-weight rule ensemble: average top three of 11 fixed experts selected by two chronological training folds' net growth, each with past-training calibrated shock gate. Diversification hypothesis reduces dependence on a single chosen rule; no ensemble weights tuned on validation.

Aggregate OHLC geometry: append normalized body, full high-low range, close-in-range over 5/20/60 sessions to close-only monthly ridge. Prior single-day/mean-candle features underperformed; hypothesis coherent multi-session candles capture path context. Same purged train MSE CV and shock gate.

Multiscale support/resistance geometry: append normalized distances to trailing high/low and range position at 21/126/252 sessions. Hypothesis monthly forecast needs long-range rebound location beyond its existing 63-session drawdown. Fixed scales, train-only purged ridge selection.

Front-loaded monthly forecast labels: exponentially weight the next 20 training log returns with fixed 5-session half-life, emphasizing nearer realized rewards while retaining smoothing. Same close-only features, purged training ridge CV, position hysteresis and shock gate; no validation-label access.

PLS1 supervised dimension reduction: train-only covariance-directed components with sequential X/y deflation, choose 1/2/4/9 components by purged late-training monthly-target MSE. Same risk gate. Hypothesis return-relevant directions improve on unsupervised PCA. Method: scikit-learn official PLS docs, undated accessed 2026-09-15, https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/cross_decomposition.html ; stdlib implementation, no package dependency.

Random Fourier nonlinear monthly forecast: 32 fixed-seed cosine features of train-standardized close-only inputs, frequency std 1/sqrt(9), ridge chosen by purged training MSE. Hypothesis smooth joint-state relations need non-axis-aligned nonlinear features. Inspired by Rahimi/Recht, NeurIPS 2007, https://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~brecht/kitchensinks.html ; adapted feature-standardized ridge, same shock gate.

Linear plus random Fourier monthly model: concatenate standardized original close-only inputs with same 32 fixed-seed cosine features. Hypothesis preserve the successful linear signal while allowing smooth nonlinear residual structure. Purged training-only ridge CV. Rahimi/Recht NeurIPS 2007, https://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~brecht/kitchensinks.html ; adapted joint regularized basis, unchanged shock gate.

Causal price-space trailing exit baseline: 22-session rolling high minus three ATR22, flat below stop and reenter only above SMA10 with a rising close. Fixed volatility-scaled stop rather than relative-volatility shock; hypothesis sustained price erosion may matter without a sudden volatility jump. No fitted parameters, close signals execute next open.

Monthly forecast with price-space risk exit: replace shock gate by fixed rolling high22 minus 3 ATR22 and SMA10 rising-close recovery, retain close-only monthly ridge and purged train-only MSE selection. Hypothesis separate slow drawdown exit from return forecast, without combining extra filters.

Episode trailing-stop overlay: original monthly ridge plus shock gate, track close-price peak during positive allocated episodes and stop at peak minus 3 ATR22. Reentry requires exceeding prior ten closes. Hypothesis protect accumulated trends when relative-volatility gate misses gradual reversals. Peaks are causal close observations, never future/execution prices; no intraday stop-fill assumption.

Conditional-noise weighted monthly ridge: weight training rows by inverse trailing-20 variance, cap relative weights at 0.1 to 10 times median, refit exact weighted intercept and covariance. Same close-only features, purged training MSE ridge selection, shock gate. Hypothesis noisy high-volatility examples should have less coefficient influence; weights use only contemporaneously known input volatility.

Robust monthly Huber regression: 12 IRLS iterations, residual cutoff 1.345 times training target standard deviation, exact weighted intercept, same ridge candidates selected by purged training MSE and original shock gate. Hypothesis residual outliers after conditioning distort coefficients; unlike label winsorization, weight depends on model error.

Approximate conditional-median monthly regression: 12 IRLS iterations with inverse absolute residual weights floored at 5% of training target standard deviation, exact weighted intercept and ridge regularization. Purged train MSE selects ridge; same close features and shock gate. Hypothesis robust central monthly drift gives cleaner signs than the mean; no validation fitting.

Training-only grouped feature selection: evaluate all seven nonempty combinations of short-return, long-trend, and volatility/drawdown groups, jointly select subset and ridge by purged late-training monthly-target MSE. Refit chosen subset on all training; unchanged risk gate. Hypothesis redundant feature groups hurt forecast stability.

Training-only grouped feature selection by trading return: same seven predetermined group subsets and ridge choices, selected by exact net log growth on purged late-training rows with prefix-calibrated shock gate and 50% drawdown cap. Hypothesis subset useful for returns may differ from MSE-optimal subset. Final validation only via runner.

Training-only forward feature selection: greedily add one of nine close-only predictors only while purged late-training monthly MSE improves, selecting ridge within each subset. Refit final subset on all training; fixed shock gate. Hypothesis a compact supervised subset avoids correlated noisy dimensions without lasso shrinkage bias.

Conditional monthly regressions by volatility state: split training rows at training median trailing-20 volatility, fit separate close-only ridge forecasts, blend current-state model 50% with pooled model. Every CV fold learns its own threshold and regressions; purged training MSE selects ridge. Hypothesis normalized predictors still have volatility-dependent return relationships; unchanged shock gate.

Joint volatility/trend conditional monthly regressions: four train-defined groups from median trailing volatility and close above/below SMA200. Shrink each local forecast toward pooled prediction by n/(n+500), minimum 80 group samples; purged training-only ridge CV. Hypothesis bear/bull volatility interactions need separate slopes rather than a shared global linear fit.

Smooth volatility mixture of monthly regressions: fit three training volatility-tercile experts; blend experts with Gaussian distance to each train median, width training volatility standard deviation, then average with pooled forecast. Train-only purged ridge CV and same shock gate. Hypothesis continuous regime weights reduce abrupt state-switch errors.

Causal state-velocity features: append five- and twenty-session differences of all nine close-only features, computed from truncated histories entirely within the 252-row observation. Hypothesis direction of change in trend/volatility state matters beyond current levels. Same monthly labels, purged training ridge CV and shock gate.

Temporal cosine return features: append four fixed discrete-cosine projections (frequencies 1,2,4,8) of last twenty volatility-normalized log returns. Hypothesis recent ordering and oscillation phase carry information that aggregated momentum ignores. Deterministic past-only basis, monthly ridge with purged training CV and unchanged gate.

Fixed nonlinear temporal filters: append eight outputs of causal two-state tanh recurrences over last sixty normalized returns, using predefined fast/slow decay and positive/negative feedback pairs. Hypothesis low-dimensional sequence memory captures reversal patterns unavailable to static random features. No fitted recurrent weights, monthly readout ridge selected only on purged training; original shock gate.

Out-of-fold daily payoff calibration: three expanding training folds generate monthly-model forecasts without label overlap; fit regularized two-parameter affine map from forecast to realized next-open daily log return. Final monthly base refits all training; frozen calibration drives same hysteresis/gate. Hypothesis monthly conditional drift requires execution-horizon calibration, distinct from correcting monthly forecast residual mean.

Out-of-fold binned daily payoff calibration: three expanding purged training folds, five equal-count forecast bins, shrink each daily log-return estimate toward training OOF mean by 100 pseudo-observations, interpolate and clamp outside centers. Hypothesis forecast magnitude and daily payoff relation is nonlinear. Final refit, same gate; all calibration labels training-only.

Out-of-fold monotone daily payoff calibration: ten equal-count training forecast bins with 100-mean pseudo-observations each, weighted pool-adjacent-violators enforces monotonicity, interpolate/clamp. Three expanding purged training folds and final full-training base refit. Hypothesis preserve forecast order while reducing noisy daily payoff mapping; unchanged gate and position threshold.

Direct recurrent allocation policy: sigmoid of nine standardized close features plus prior latent allocation; exact forward sensitivities through recurrence, weight drift, turnover and terminal liquidation optimize annualized net log growth. Purged late-training return selects penalty and 100/300 steps; no leverage, no risk gate. Inspired by Moody/Saffell July 2001 https://people.idsia.ch/~juergen/rnnaissance2003talks/MoodySaffellTNN01.pdf ; adapted simple recurrent model, hypothesis memory improves transaction-aware policy over feedforward baseline.

Direct recurrent allocation with integrated shock gate: same causal sigmoid-memory policy and exact forward gradient of net log growth, but multiply allocations by train-calibrated shock gate inside training objective and training CV as well as inference. Prefix training alone calibrates CV thresholds. Hypothesis jointly learning exposure around risk-off states outperforms applying gate only after optimization. Moody/Saffell July 2001 https://people.idsia.ch/~juergen/rnnaissance2003talks/MoodySaffellTNN01.pdf ; adapted recurrent direct policy.

Rule-based trend/oscillation switch: ADX14 above 25 follows positive-vs-negative directional movement; below 20 buys CCI20 below -100 and exits above zero; intermediate state retains position. Own combined hypothesis, conventional fixed thresholds, causal OHLC only, next-open execution. Indicators: Fidelity DMI/CCI guides, undated accessed 2026-09-15, https://www.fidelity.com/learning-center/trading-investing/technical-analysis/technical-indicator-guide/DMI and https://www.fidelity.com/learning-center/trading-investing/technical-analysis/technical-indicator-guide/cci .

Monthly ridge with directional-movement context: append DI14 spread, ADX14 strength and their interaction to original close-only model. Hypothesis high/low trend persistence adds information beyond close trend slopes. Same purged train ridge CV and shock gate. Indicators: Fidelity DMI/CCI guides, undated accessed 2026-09-15, https://www.fidelity.com/learning-center/trading-investing/technical-analysis/technical-indicator-guide/DMI and https://www.fidelity.com/learning-center/trading-investing/technical-analysis/technical-indicator-guide/cci .

Monthly ridge with trend-conditioned oscillator context: add DI spread, ADX strength, signed trend strength, CCI20, five-session CCI change and CCI-times-ADX. Hypothesis an extreme oscillator can mean continuation under strong trend and reversal otherwise; learned only from training, fixed model protocol. Indicators: Fidelity DMI/CCI guides, undated accessed 2026-09-15, https://www.fidelity.com/learning-center/trading-investing/technical-analysis/technical-indicator-guide/DMI and https://www.fidelity.com/learning-center/trading-investing/technical-analysis/technical-indicator-guide/cci .

Derivative-free binary policy learning via cross-entropy method: diagonal Gaussian population32 elite8, fixed seed, optimize exact cost-adjusted log growth with 50% drawdown constraint. Nine standardized inputs, fixed +/-0.25 signal hysteresis; late purged training selects 10/20/30 generations then refit. Hypothesis direct search avoids sigmoid-gradient near-full-investment plateaus. No risk gate. Inspired by de Boer/Kroese/Mannor/Rubinstein 2005, https://people.smp.uq.edu.au/DirkKroese/ps/aortut.pdf .

Cross-entropy binary policy learning with integrated shock gate: same deterministic population search and exact net-growth objective, multiply positions by prefix-trained shock gate in fitting, training CV and final inference. Hypothesis discontinuous entry/exit plus risk-off structure benefits from derivative-free optimization; final validation never accessed during policy fitting. Inspired by de Boer/Kroese/Mannor/Rubinstein 2005, https://people.smp.uq.edu.au/DirkKroese/ps/aortut.pdf .

Training-only stacked forecast horizons: 1/5/20/60-session ridge models generate three expanding-fold OOF predictions; each base model chooses ridge on its own purged prefix. Choose among 35 convex quarter-step mixtures by OOF monthly-target MSE, refit full training. Hypothesis learned horizon mixture improves on prior equal weekly/monthly/quarterly blend. All stacking labels training-only; unchanged shock gate.

Return-selected training-only horizon stack: same four purged nested ridge forecasts and 35 convex mixtures, choose mixture by exact daily net log growth with prefix-calibrated shock gate on three OOF training folds, including turnover, fold liquidation and drawdown cap. Hypothesis forecast horizon weights should reflect trading payoff rather than target MSE; full-training refit then fixed validation inference.

Arithmetic daily-payoff forecast with explicit volatility drag: fit monthly average of simple daily forward returns instead of log returns, then subtract half contemporaneous daily variance before allocation to approximate geometric drift. Same nine causal close features, purged train ridge CV, hysteresis and shock gate. Hypothesis separating conditional arithmetic payoff and known variance drag avoids their confounding in one log-return regression; approximation, not exact utility.

Compounded monthly-payoff target: ridge learns realized 20-session compounded simple return divided by 20, converts predicted horizon payoff back to per-session log scale for allocation. Same model and purged training selection. Hypothesis expected holding-period wealth weights strong trends differently from averaging daily log rewards; final ranking still exact frozen net CAGR.

Path-risk-adjusted monthly training target: subtract half within-future-window daily log-return variance from mean monthly log drift when constructing training labels. Variance is training-label information only and is never computed from future observations at allocation. Hypothesis penalizing unstable training return paths yields more reliable positive forecasts while preserving original position/risk execution.

Nonoverlapping shock baseline: compare fast last-five return volatility with preceding sixty returns excluding those five, instead of overlapping 5/60 windows. Relearn 95/70 percentile thresholds solely on training; same monthly predictor and price/recovery rules. Hypothesis fast shocks should not simultaneously inflate their own reference volatility.

Robust pre-shock baseline: last-five standard deviation divided by 1.4826 median absolute deviation of preceding sixty returns, floor .001; train calibrates same 95/70 quantiles. Same monthly predictor and gate transition rules. Hypothesis historical isolated extremes mask new shocks in standard-deviation reference; robust reference resists that masking.

Slower forecast feature normalization: use contemporaneous sixty-session close volatility in the nine predictor normalization terms and volatility feature rather than twenty-session volatility, retain five-session numerator and original independent shock gate. Hypothesis month-ahead forecasts need a more stable risk scale; all model fitting and ridge selection remain purged training-only.

Local residual correction to monthly ridge: retain global forecast then add Gaussian-distance weighted training residual mean from 100 nearest standardized training states, shrunk by 100 zero-residual pseudo-observations. Unlike earlier raw-neighbor averaging, preserve global trend slopes and correct only local bias. Purged training CV refits entire model for each ridge; unchanged shock gate.

Query-local linear monthly forecasting: 256 nearest standardized training states, Gaussian distance weights, exact local weighted intercept and ridge1 slopes, average with globally fitted forecast. Hypothesis conditional slopes need smooth multivariate locality beyond hard volatility/trend groups. Global ridge chosen by purged training MSE of combined predictor; local data always training-only, unchanged shock gate.

Purged delete-block monthly ensemble: eight deterministic contiguous training blocks, each member omits one block plus preceding 19 overlapping target starts; average forecasts. Ridge chosen using same purged chronological inner training fold. Hypothesis delete-block aggregation is less noisy than earlier moving-block bootstrap while reducing dependence on individual market episodes; original close features and shock gate.

Robust median delete-block monthly ensemble: same eight purged leave-block-out training regressions, median forecast rather than mean. Hypothesis a few influential training episodes distort signs and median aggregation resists them. Train-only chronological ridge CV, unchanged features, hysteresis and shock gate.

Variance-clock training horizon: average future training log returns over round(20*(1%/current-vol20)^2) sessions, bounded 5 to 60. High-volatility states use shorter forecasts and low-volatility states longer; omit final59 rows and purge61 before internal CV. Fixed reference volatility, no validation fitting. Hypothesis constant risk-time target is more stable than fixed monthly calendar horizon; original execution gate/hysteresis retained.

Adaptive-moving-average trend baseline: Kaufman efficiency length10, fast2/slow30, close-vs-KAMA hysteresis band half trailing daily volatility in price units. Hypothesis adapt smoothing to path efficiency to reduce fixed-SMA lag/whipsaw; no fitting, no date rules. TradingView KAMA method docs, undated accessed2026-09-15 https://www.tradingview.com/support/solutions/43000773012-kaufman-s-adaptive-moving-average-kama/ .

KAMA state features for monthly ridge: append volatility-normalized price deviation, five-session adaptive-average slope and current adaptive smoothing coefficient. Same training-only purged ridge CV and shock gate. Hypothesis learned forecast can use adaptive trend information without rigid crossing rules. TradingView KAMA method docs, undated accessed2026-09-15 https://www.tradingview.com/support/solutions/43000773012-kaufman-s-adaptive-moving-average-kama/ .

Hull moving-average monthly features: append normalized close deviation and five-session slope of HMA20 and HMA60, using weighted-average lag compensation and rounded square-root smoothing. Hypothesis low-lag trend features add information beyond SMA200 and normalized raw momentum. Same purged training CV/gate. Fidelity HMA docs, undated accessed2026-09-15 https://www.fidelity.com/learning-center/trading-investing/technical-analysis/technical-indicator-guide/hull-moving-average .

Training empirical-rank Gaussianization: replace all nine close-only predictor values with normal quantiles of their training empirical marginal CDF, midrank ties and tail probability clamp 0.001/0.999. Fold-specific transforms, purged training ridge CV, unchanged monthly labels and shock gate. Hypothesis rank-based features reduce sensitivity to heavy-tailed magnitude changes while preserving ordering.

Mixed magnitude/rank monthly model: concatenate original nine close-only features with their train-empirical Gaussian rank transforms. Hypothesis keep informative magnitude variation while allowing different nonlinear responses across common and extreme states. Entire transform fitted within each purged training fold, then full refit; unchanged original shock gate.

GARCH-normalized innovation shock gate: fit stationary GARCH(1,1) to training close log returns by Gaussian likelihood over fixed alpha/beta candidates, variance-target intercept. Gate score is RMS of last five standardized innovations, each normalized by variance forecast before that return; train95/70 quantiles and original price/recovery rules. Hypothesis surprise relative to conditional volatility is more useful than raw fast/slow volatility; monthly return model unchanged. Method inspiration: Bollerslev, Journal of Econometrics April1986, https://doi.org/10.1016/0304-4076(86)90063-1 ; variance targeting plus finite training likelihood search is an adapted implementation.

GARCH forecast-volatility shock gate: same train-fitted variance model, risk score is sqrt(next conditional variance / mean previous60 conditional variances). Same train95/70 quantiles, monthly forecast and gate transitions. Hypothesis modeled volatility persistence identifies risky regimes after transient innovations fade; recursion uses only trailing252 closes. Method inspiration: Bollerslev, Journal of Econometrics April1986, https://doi.org/10.1016/0304-4076(86)90063-1 ; variance targeting plus finite training likelihood search is an adapted implementation.

Learned nonlinear monthly predictor: one tanh hidden layer with eight units, deterministic seed, train-standardized inputs/targets, minibatch32 SGD and mild weight decay. Purged late-training monthly MSE selects 200/600/1200 updates, then full-training refit; original shock gate. Hypothesis learned nonlinear projections improve beyond fixed random features; no validation gradient or fitting.

Learned nonlinear residual monthly predictor: same eight-unit tanh network models residual around fixed ridge0.1 linear skip forecast, preserving linear structure while learning smooth interactions. Purged training early stopping selects update count, all full-training refits deterministic; original shock gate. Hypothesis residual initialization is more stable than an entirely nonlinear signal.

Linear/nonlinear forecast diversification: equal-average original purged-CV monthly ridge forecast and independently trained eight-unit tanh monthly forecast, then apply common signal hysteresis and shock gate. Both base model selection procedures use training only; fixed 50/50 weight. Hypothesis different inductive biases reduce forecast sign errors despite neither nonlinear model individually exceeding current champion.

Linear/nonlinear allocation diversification: same independently fitted monthly ridge and tanh models, keep separate binary signal hysteresis states and average their allocations before the shared shock gate. Hypothesis partial exposure on model disagreement can retain profitable periods lost by averaging noisy forecast magnitudes. Fixed equal weights, no validation-fit stacking.

Noise-regularized linear/nonlinear ensemble: add independent Gaussian noise sd0.1 to standardized neural training inputs only, preserving minibatch RNG sequence and clean inference. Original ridge, fixed 50/50 forecast blend, purged training early stopping and shock gate unchanged. Hypothesis local input smoothing stabilizes neural decisions without adding features or tuning validation weights.

Robust-loss linear/nonlinear ensemble: neural minibatch gradients use Huber derivative cutoff1.345 in standardized target units; keep original clean inputs, ridge forecast, equal blend, purged training MSE early stopping and risk gate. Hypothesis downweighting rare extreme residuals yields a more useful nonlinear complement to ridge.

Ensemble-aware neural early stopping: select neural 200/600/1200-step checkpoint by MSE of its equal forecast blend with a ridge model fitted to exactly the corresponding purged training prefix. Then refit both full-training models. Hypothesis the most useful ensemble member need not minimize its own standalone error; fixed equal blend, unchanged architecture/gate, no validation fitting.

Fixed three-seed neural averaging with noisy inputs: average all networks seeded 6047/6048/6049 without seed selection; choose their shared 200/600/1200 checkpoint using purged training mean-forecast MSE. Equal blend with unchanged ridge and shock gate. Hypothesis averaging initialization and minibatch variation stabilizes the nonlinear complement; no validation-fitted seeds or weights.

Training checkpoint prediction averaging: average all noisy-neural checkpoints up to 200,600,1200, selecting cumulative endpoint solely by purged training MSE then refitting all retained checkpoints. Fixed equal ridge blend and shock gate. Hypothesis temporal averaging along one training trajectory reduces forecast variance without selecting lucky seeds.

Nonoverlapping-target neural minibatches: each step sample 32 distinct training starts from one randomly chosen 20-session phase, so no monthly forward-label windows overlap within the batch. Preserve noisy-input architecture, train-only checkpoint selection, equal ridge blend and gate. Hypothesis reducing duplicated target information per gradient gives a more useful nonlinear estimate.

OHLC variance shock gate: replace close-return standard-deviation ratio with sqrt(mean5/mean60) of Rogers-Satchell intraday variance plus squared overnight gaps; training 95/70 quantiles and all forecast components unchanged. Hypothesis within-session path variation detects risk shifts hidden in closes. Method inspiration Rogers and Satchell, November 1991, https://www.skokholm.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2016/01/R_Satchell_HLOC.pdf ; overnight squared gaps are our additional risk proxy, not an assertion of the paper's estimator.

Variance decomposition forecast features: append RS intraday volatility relative to close volatility, log intraday variance5/60 and overnight energy share20 to both ridge and noisy neural predictors; preserve original close-volatility shock gate. Hypothesis separating intraday oscillation from overnight moves helps distinguish drift from noisy risk. Method inspiration Rogers and Satchell, November 1991, https://www.skokholm.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2016/01/R_Satchell_HLOC.pdf ; overnight squared gaps are our additional risk proxy, not an assertion of the paper's estimator.

OHLC-normalized forecast features: replace close-based 20/5-day volatility normalization in the existing nine features with square-root average RS-plus-overnight energy at identical horizons. Preserve original independent close-return shock gate and training-only model fitting. Hypothesis path-based scale estimates stabilize momentum and distance predictors. Method inspiration Rogers and Satchell, November 1991, https://www.skokholm.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2016/01/R_Satchell_HLOC.pdf ; overnight squared gaps are our additional risk proxy, not an assertion of the paper's estimator.

Specialist nonlinear reversal expert: retain monthly ridge on nine close features; train the noisy neural member only on one/five-day returns, short-to-medium volatility ratio, volatility level and normalized drawdown. Fixed equal monthly forecast blend and shock gate, purged train-only early stopping. Hypothesis feature specialization reduces redundant long-trend learning and exposes nonlinear short-run effects.

Specialist nonlinear intraday expert: retain existing monthly close-feature ridge; train neural member only on short/medium volatility ratio, volatility level, latest candle close location, body, overnight gap and range. Fixed equal forecast blend and original gate, no additional data. Hypothesis a distinct OHLC information set provides more complementary nonlinear forecasts than sharing all close features.

Mixed-horizon linear/neural forecasts: original monthly ridge plus noisy neural five-session mean-log target, equal daily-unit forecast blend. Neural checkpoint selection uses purged training split with six-row gap; original features, architecture and shock gate. Hypothesis nonlinear short-horizon response complements slower linear expected returns; horizons and blend predetermined without validation fitting.

Purged three-fold training stack, convex forecast blend: fit base ridge/noisy-neural ensemble on expanding training prefixes ending21 rows before 50/65/80 percent boundaries; collect monthly-target OOF forecasts in later training blocks. Analytically fit clipped ridge weight0..1 by MSE with 10-percent quadratic shrink toward equal weights. Refit base full train, freeze blend and gate. Hypothesis complementary models merit a training-estimated blend.

Purged three-fold residual calibration: same expanding 50/65/80-percent training-prefix OOF predictions with21-row purge; fit ridge penalty1 on the two forecasts to predict residual of their equal blend against monthly log labels. Full-training base refit; freeze affine correction. Hypothesis conservative bias/scale calibration corrects mismatch between raw models and executable expected returns without fitting validation data.

Purged three-fold economic hysteresis selection: base ensemble fit only on expanding prefixes with21-row purge, then select threshold among0,round-trip-cost/20,2.5bp,5bp using aggregate net log growth on three later training blocks with the prefix-trained shock gate, next-open labels, 0.05-percent switching and terminal costs. Full-training base refit; frozen threshold. Hypothesis decision threshold should reflect realized training utility rather than forecast MSE alone.

Shared-trunk multi-horizon neural learning: eight tanh hidden units jointly predict standardized 20/5/1-session mean-log training targets with equally weighted squared losses; use only monthly output in fixed equal blend with original ridge. Noisy inputs, 200/600/1200 early stopping on purged monthly training MSE, unchanged shock gate. Hypothesis auxiliary shorter horizons regularize return representation without replacing the monthly decision target.

Shared-trunk return/risk auxiliary learning: same eight-unit noisy neural trunk jointly predicts monthly mean log return, future20-session log-return volatility and downside RMS, each standardized from fitting rows. Use only return output with unchanged ridge/gate; purge21 and early stop by monthly training MSE. Hypothesis learning future dispersion jointly improves useful state representation; auxiliary labels exist only inside training data.

Shared multi-horizon forecast averaging: jointly train 20/5/1-session daily-unit log-return heads sharing an eight-tanh-unit noisy trunk; average all three daily-return predictions for the neural forecast, then equal blend with monthly ridge. Select checkpoint by purged training monthly MSE of this mean forecast. Hypothesis shared representation plus horizon diversification improves response while preserving fixed ex-ante combination weights.

Payoff-weighted neural sign classification: replace neural squared-error target with monthly-return sign and logistic loss weighted by absolute monthly mean log return. Convert probability to signed forecast using fitting-sample average absolute return, blend equally with original ridge. Noisy inputs and purged train MSE checkpoint selection unchanged. Hypothesis economically weighted directional learning better prioritizes decisions than fitting return magnitude; global magnitude conversion is an explicit approximation.

Conditional-magnitude payoff-weighted neural classifier: use absolute-return-weighted logistic sign loss, then scale signed probability by a ridge penalty1 prediction of conditional absolute monthly return fitted on the same training rows. Equal original ridge blend and unchanged gate. Hypothesis estimating state-dependent magnitude corrects the constant-magnitude approximation of weighted directional forecasts; all fitting and early stopping remain training-only.

Standalone payoff-weighted neural timing: use monthly sign logistic loss weighted by absolute monthly mean log return, global-magnitude signed-probability forecast and original shock gate, without ridge forecast blending. Training-only purged checkpoint selection. Hypothesis an economically weighted directional classifier can serve as an independent timing family rather than only an ensemble component.

Nonlinear direct-utility policy: replace earlier linear sigmoid policy with eight tanh hidden units and sigmoid weight0..1. Full chronological gradient ascent on exact daily net-log wealth including drifted prior weights, switching costs and final liquidation; fixed weight decay.01, select50/150 iterations on purged later training net growth. No external shock gate. Hypothesis optimizing executable economic utility directly learns nonlinear allocations missed by return forecasting. Inspired by direct utility optimization in Moody and Saffell, July2001, https://people.idsia.ch/~juergen/rnnaissance2003talks/MoodySaffellTNN01.pdf ; this candidate is a feedforward adaptation, not a paper reproduction.

Shock-aware nonlinear direct-utility policy: eight-tanh sigmoid allocation trained by exact chronological net-log-wealth gradient with training-calibrated shock gate inside objective. Include drift, switching and liquidation derivatives, fixed penalty.01, training-only50/150 checkpoint selection with two-row purge. Hypothesis nonlinear risk-conditioned utility training yields useful state-dependent exposure. Inspired by direct utility optimization in Moody and Saffell, July2001, https://people.idsia.ch/~juergen/rnnaissance2003talks/MoodySaffellTNN01.pdf ; this candidate is a feedforward adaptation, not a paper reproduction.

Discrete execution of nonlinear utility policy: same shock-aware eight-tanh direct-net-growth training, but select checkpoint and execute through fixed0.6/0.4 probability hysteresis to index/cash. Fixed penalty.01 and purged training-only checkpoint choice. Hypothesis converting smooth allocation preferences into persistent binary exposure preserves growth while reducing small trades; optimize smooth surrogate but select using actual discrete training execution. Inspired by direct utility optimization in Moody and Saffell, July2001, https://people.idsia.ch/~juergen/rnnaissance2003talks/MoodySaffellTNN01.pdf ; this candidate is a feedforward adaptation, not a paper reproduction.

Causal L1 trend timing: fit piecewise-linear trend to latest64 log closes normalized by trailing20 volatility, fixed L1 curvature penalty10 and ADMM rho10; buy/cash according to latest three-session endpoint slope with ±0.005 normalized hysteresis. No fitting or dates, no shock gate. Hypothesis sparse slope changes identify persistent direction with fewer false reversals. Source Kim, Koh, Boyd and Gorinevsky, SIAM Review May2009, https://stanford.edu/~boyd/papers/l1_trend_filter.html ; causal rolling-endpoint adaptation with a fixed120-step ADMM approximation, not a full-sample retrospective smoother.

Causal L1 trend plus volatility-break gate: same fixed64-session piecewise-linear endpoint-slope timing, combined with original training95/70 close-volatility shock gate. Hypothesis trend segmentation and abrupt-risk detection provide complementary exits. Source Kim, Koh, Boyd and Gorinevsky, SIAM Review May2009, https://stanford.edu/~boyd/papers/l1_trend_filter.html ; causal rolling-endpoint adaptation with a fixed120-step ADMM approximation, not a full-sample retrospective smoother.

L1 trend representation in learned ensemble: append normalized recent endpoint slope, close-minus-filtered endpoint and slope change to the existing ridge/noisy-neural monthly forecasters. Preserve equal blend, purged training checkpoint choice and original gate. Hypothesis piecewise-linear trend geometry adds regime information beyond moving averages. Source Kim, Koh, Boyd and Gorinevsky, SIAM Review May2009, https://stanford.edu/~boyd/papers/l1_trend_filter.html ; causal rolling-endpoint adaptation with a fixed120-step ADMM approximation, not a full-sample retrospective smoother.

Ordered daily-path neural representation: preserve original nine-feature monthly ridge, but feed neural member the latest20 ordered one-session log returns normalized by current20 volatility, plus63 momentum, price/SMA200, SMA50/SMA200 and volatility. Noisy-input eight-unit model, train-only early stopping, equal blend and gate unchanged. Hypothesis learned short path motifs contain information lost by aggregate indicators.

Ordered weekly-block neural representation: neural member receives12 disjoint five-session normalized log-return blocks covering latest60 sessions, ordered oldest to newest, plus four slow trend/volatility features; original ridge and gate unchanged. Fixed monthly target and equal blend. Hypothesis aggregating within weeks suppresses daily noise while retaining the order of medium-term gains and losses.

Multiscale return-acceleration neural representation: append Haar-style differences between recent and preceding half-window log returns at2/4/8/16/32/64/128 sessions to the original nine neural inputs; scale by current volatility times square-root horizon. Keep ridge inputs unchanged. Hypothesis nonlinear combinations of accelerating and decelerating trends at distinct scales complement simple cumulative momentum.

Residual linear model tree: fit monthly global ridge then split its training residuals using largest squared-error mean reduction over feature terciles, depth2/minleaf200. Each leaf fits a ridge residual model, prediction shrunk by n/(n+500) toward global ridge. Preserve purged training ridge selection and original shock gate. Hypothesis local slopes capture regime-specific responses that constant regression trees miss.

Residual linear model forest: average eight depth2/minleaf200 model trees, each considering four randomly sampled features per split with a fixed seed; leaf ridge residual correction shrunk by n/(n+500). Global monthly ridge and shock gate unchanged, ridge selected only on purged later training data. Hypothesis averaging alternative regime partitions reduces instability of local linear forecasts.

Full-target local linear tree with pooling: partition by global-ridge residual mean separation, but fit full monthly return models inside depth2/minleaf200 leaves and interpolate local/global predictions using n/(n+500). Original train-only ridge choice and risk gate. Hypothesis jointly changing local intercept and slopes handles regime variation better than an additive residual model.

Training-covariance whitening for neural inputs: whiten the nine standardized/clipped neural features using fitting-only covariance shrunk10 percent toward identity and its Cholesky factor, then clip whitened coordinates. Preserve noisy training, ridge inputs, equal blend, gate and purged checkpoint selection. Hypothesis decorrelating redundant trend features improves nonlinear optimization and makes isotropic input noise more meaningful.

Feature dropout neural regularization: replace additive Gaussian input noise with independent10-percent inverted feature masking during neural training, clean inference and unchanged minibatch RNG; original ridge, equal blend and gate retained. Hypothesis preventing dependence on any one indicator produces a more stable nonlinear complement under changing market states.

Hidden-unit dropout neural regularization: retain original Gaussian input perturbation and independently mask10 percent of hidden activations using inverted scaling with matching backprop derivatives; clean inference, original ridge and gate. Hypothesis discouraging hidden-unit coadaptation regularizes nonlinear interactions without changing available indicators or searching validation-tuned penalties.

Group-wise feature dropout: jointly mask four predeclared neural feature groups (short reversal, slow trend, volatility, drawdown) with10-percent probability and inverted scaling instead of independently masking individual coordinates. Keep original ridge, equal blend, gate and purged checkpoint selection. Hypothesis preserving relationships within correlated indicators while withholding entire information groups improves robustness.

Analytical dropout regularization for ridge member: add diagonal covariance penalty p/(1-p) times standardized feature second moment, p=.1, to the ridge normal equations. Keep neural feature dropout, equal forecast blend and gate; base ridge penalty still selected only on purged training data. Hypothesis extending missing-feature robustness to the linear member improves the combined forecast.

Exhaustive leave-one-feature-out neural ensemble: train nine fixed eight-hidden-unit networks, each with one of the nine indicators permanently masked during fitting and inference; equal-average every member, no random subset or seed selection. Select shared checkpoint by purged training ensemble MSE, full refit, equal blend with unchanged ridge/gate. Hypothesis explicit feature-subset averaging tests whether stochastic input dropout gains survive deterministic model averaging.

Softsign neural interactions: replace tanh hidden activation and derivative with softsign x/(1+abs(x)), keeping input dropout, initialization, training schedule, purged checkpoint choice, equal ridge blend and shock gate. Hypothesis polynomial rather than exponential saturation retains sensitivity to unusually strong standardized signals without unbounded activations.

Closed-form neural readout refinement: after each200/600/1200 neural checkpoint, fit a penalty0.1 ridge readout on its eight clean hidden activations and monthly training labels; choose checkpoint by purged training MSE, full refit. Preserve feature-dropout hidden training and equal original-ridge blend/gate. Hypothesis solving the final layer directly reduces optimization error left by stochastic gradient training.
