Joint hidden/raw closed-form readout: after dropout neural training, fit a penalty0.1 ridge on the concatenation of eight learned hidden activations and nine standardized original inputs. Purged train-only checkpoint choice, original ridge member/equal blend/gate unchanged. Hypothesis a jointly fitted linear path plus learned interactions improves calibration relative to freezing separate linear and neural readouts.

Gaussian variance-change scan gate: for trailing60 log returns, maximize zero-mean variance-segmentation likelihood ratio across candidate recent block lengths5/10/20/30, retaining only increases in recent energy. Use square-root statistic with training95/70 quantiles and original price-break/recovery conditions; dropout ensemble unchanged. Hypothesis scanning possible onset ages detects persistent volatility transitions missed by one fixed ratio. Statistic derived from Gaussian log likelihood; no external data.

Downward joint mean/variance change gate: maximize Gaussian two-segment versus pooled log-likelihood ratio over trailing60 returns and recent lengths5/10/20/30, retaining negative recent means. Use square-root score with original training quantile calibration and price confirmation. Hypothesis identifying a downward distribution shift captures sustained risk even when close-volatility ratios are moderate. Analytical Gaussian likelihood construction, training-only thresholds.

Distribution-change forecast representation: add one-sided variance-change likelihood score, negative-mean joint-change score and largest absolute signed two-sample mean-shift statistic from trailing60 log returns to both dropout-neural and ridge forecasts. Keep original volatility gate and fixed equal blend. Hypothesis providing graded evidence of distribution shifts lets training learn when changes imply reversal versus continuation; all scans use past history only.

Regime-balanced neural training: form four training-only groups by price above/below SMA200 and volatility above/below fitting-sample median, then sample groups uniformly and observations uniformly within group. Keep feature dropout, monthly target, purged MSE checkpoint choice and original ridge/gate. Hypothesis giving rarer weak-trend regimes equal learning weight improves nonlinear decisions beyond predominantly rising-market training examples.

Chronologically stratified neural minibatches: split fitting rows into eight contiguous equal blocks and draw four observations per block for every32-example update. All blocks and rows remain within fitting prefix; original monthly labels, feature dropout, ridge blend and gate unchanged. Hypothesis each update seeing diverse training eras reduces gradient imbalance without changing the expected empirical loss.

Loss-adaptive chronological neural sampling: split fitting rows into four contiguous blocks and sample blocks proportional to exponentially tracked standardized squared-error loss, clipped0.25..4, with within-block uniform sampling. Loss tracking uses only sampled training errors and starts equally. Preserve feature dropout, purged checkpoint choice and ridge/gate. Hypothesis spending more updates on persistently poorly fitted training regimes improves robustness to heterogeneous dynamics.

Causal singular-spectrum trend timing: form a lagged log-price trajectory matrix from latest64 closes, reconstruct rank2 signal by diagonal averaging, extrapolate one point using recurrent SSA coefficients and trade the reconstructed endpoint slope with fixed normalized hysteresis. Hypothesis low-rank trend/cycle extraction identifies persistent direction without selecting calendar regimes. Method source Golyandina/Korobeynikov, submitted2012-06-28, https://arxiv.org/abs/1206.6910 ; fixed rolling64 observations, lag16/rank2,40-step orthogonalized power approximation. Reconstruction is redone using past observations only.

Causal singular-spectrum trend with shock gate: fixed rank2 recurrent SSA endpoint direction combined with original training-calibrated volatility-break gate. Hypothesis latent trend extrapolation and abrupt-risk detection cover different failure modes. Method source Golyandina/Korobeynikov, submitted2012-06-28, https://arxiv.org/abs/1206.6910 ; fixed rolling64 observations, lag16/rank2,40-step orthogonalized power approximation. Reconstruction is redone using past observations only.

Singular-spectrum features for dropout ensemble: add reconstructed next-step slope, next forecast minus current observed log-price and explained trajectory energy fraction to both monthly ridge/neural inputs. Keep equal blend, purged training fitting and original gate. Hypothesis learned models can distinguish smooth latent continuation from endpoint noise using these features. Method source Golyandina/Korobeynikov, submitted2012-06-28, https://arxiv.org/abs/1206.6910 ; fixed rolling64 observations, lag16/rank2,40-step orthogonalized power approximation. Reconstruction is redone using past observations only.

Combine stochastic and exhaustive feature robustness: retain original ridge at50-percent forecast weight and split remaining50 percent equally between feature-dropout neural model and equal-averaged nine leave-one-feature-out neural models. Each neural branch chooses checkpoints on purged training MSE independently; weights fixed, gate unchanged. Hypothesis complementary regularization methods reduce branch-specific prediction errors.

Median aggregation of leave-one-feature-out experts: keep all nine deterministic masked-feature neural models and use their median prediction instead of mean, including during purged training checkpoint selection. Equal blend with unchanged original ridge and gate. Hypothesis an extreme forecast caused by removal of one important indicator should not dominate the ensemble.

Conditional-quantile neural expectation: train five shared-hidden monthly log-return quantile heads at probabilities0.1/0.3/0.5/0.7/0.9 using pinball loss and input dropout; average their daily-unit quantile predictions as a midpoint approximation to conditional mean. Purged training-MSE checkpoint selection, equal original-ridge blend and gate unchanged. Hypothesis learning return distribution shape reduces sensitivity to extreme labels compared with squared-error mean fitting.

Conditional-quantile neural expectation: train five shared-hidden monthly log-return quantile heads at probabilities0.1/0.3/0.5/0.7/0.9 using pinball loss and input dropout; average their daily-unit quantile predictions as a midpoint approximation to conditional mean. Purged training-MSE checkpoint selection, equal original-ridge blend and gate unchanged. Hypothesis learning return distribution shape reduces sensitivity to extreme labels compared with squared-error mean fitting. Correct the five-head bias-gradient buffer dimension; previous attempt crashed before evaluation. Small in-memory shape check verifies all five heads execute.

Return-priority risk-gate ablation: use the feature-dropout ridge/neural forecast and its original position hysteresis directly, without the external volatility gate. Frozen max-drawdown constraint remains50 percent in evaluator. Hypothesis the stronger learned forecaster may avoid sufficient losses by itself while the gate suppresses profitable high-volatility exposure; no model or protocol changes.

Partial exposure during volatility alarms: preserve dropout ensemble decisions and original risk-state transitions but retain half of the forecast-requested index position while the shock gate is off. Fully exposed when gate on, never leveraged. Hypothesis accepting more risk within the fixed50-percent drawdown cap can preserve rebound participation rather than forcing all alarm periods to cash; one predetermined midpoint exposure, not a validation grid.

Continuous variance-scaled alarm exposure: preserve dropout forecast and risk-state transitions; when gate is off, multiply requested exposure by min(1,(training recovery ratio/current short-long volatility ratio)^2), restoring full exposure when gate turns on. Hypothesis proportional risk reduction uses magnitude of the alarm and retains some positive-forecast participation while respecting0..1 holdings.

Era-demeaned neural training labels: within each fitting call, split monthly labels into four contiguous blocks, subtract each block mean and restore the overall fitting mean before neural optimization. Evaluation/early stopping still compares predictions with untouched later-training labels. Original ridge and gate unchanged. Hypothesis suppressing era-specific return-level shifts encourages reusable within-era nonlinear patterns instead of incidental era correlations.

Within-era fixed-effects ridge slopes: estimate ridge covariance and cross-moments after demeaning standardized features and monthly targets inside four fitting-only chronological blocks; deploy slopes around full-fitting feature means and global target mean. Neural dropout branch keeps original labels/normalization, equal blend and gate. Hypothesis separating era intercept shifts from predictive slopes improves transfer of the linear member.

Combined era-adjusted forecasting: fit ridge slopes from within-era centered feature/target moments and train dropout neural model on block-demeaned monthly labels with global mean restored. Each fitting call derives its own four blocks entirely inside its training prefix; preserve purged original-target checkpoint evaluation and gate. Hypothesis removing nuisance era levels in both branches improves stable conditional-return estimation.

Depth-two symmetric gradient boosting: fit monthly mean-log labels with up to120 additive depth2 trees, choosing global symmetric splits from fitting-only feature quartiles, minleaf40, leaf shrinkage50 and learning rate.05. Choose20/60/120 trees by purged training MSE; original shock gate. Hypothesis learned two-feature interactions overcome the limited expressiveness of earlier boosted stumps.

Ridge and depth-two boosted-tree forecast blend: equal-average independently training-selected monthly ridge and symmetric depth2 boosting predictions, preserving original hysteresis and gate. Boosted trees use fixed minleaf40/shrinkage50/rate.05 and purged train checkpoint selection. Hypothesis local threshold interactions provide a complementary predictor to global linear slopes.

Robust depth-two boosting ensemble: clip boosting pseudo-residuals at1.345 times fitting-target standard deviation, with otherwise identical symmetric-tree construction, purged training checkpoint selection and equal ridge blend. Hypothesis bounded residual influence prevents unusual training episodes from dominating interaction splits.

Volatility-unit neural targets: divide each monthly mean-log training target by its observation's trailing20 close volatility, fit the dropout neural predictor in those units, and multiply its forecast by the current observable volatility at inference. Select checkpoints against original-unit labels on purged later training data. Original ridge and shock gate unchanged. Hypothesis predicting standardized reward separates direction from changing return scale.

Heteroskedastic neural loss weighting: retain original return units but weight neural squared errors inversely to current trailing20 volatility squared, relative to fitting-sample median and clipped0.25..4 then mean-normalized. Keep dropout, purged unweighted MSE checkpoint choice, ridge blend and gate. Hypothesis bounded variance weighting prevents noisy observations from dominating conditional-mean estimation without altering prediction units.

Global training mixup with feature dropout: convexly combine pairs of standardized training examples and their monthly targets using Beta(.2,.2) coefficients, then apply original input dropout. Independent augmentation RNG preserves primary minibatch selection; clean inference, purged checkpoint choice and ridge/gate unchanged. Hypothesis enforcing smoother behavior between training states improves generalization. Source Zhang et al., submitted2017-10-25, https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.09412 .

Time-local training mixup: constrain each paired example to within20 training rows of the original before convex feature/label interpolation, retaining Beta(.2,.2), dropout and other original settings. Hypothesis local interpolation avoids unrealistic mixtures of distant market regimes while smoothing overlapping monthly targets. Adaptation of Zhang et al., submitted2017-10-25, https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.09412 ; pairs never cross the fitting-prefix boundary.

Adversarial feature smoothing during neural training: after dropout, perturb each active standardized feature by0.05 along the sign of its current squared-error gradient, then train on the perturbed input; masked features remain zero, inference remains clean. Original ridge/gate and purged checkpoint selection. Hypothesis reducing sensitivity to worst-direction small indicator errors improves stability. Method inspiration Goodfellow et al., submitted2014-12-20, https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.6572 ; regression adaptation.

Bipower shock gate: use square-root adjacent absolute-return products for short/long volatility ratio with unchanged train95/70 calibration and price confirmations. Hypothesis persistence-sensitive volatility separates repeated stress from isolated moves. Ridge/dropout forecast unchanged. Source Barndorff-Nielsen and Shephard (2004), https://shephard.scholars.harvard.edu/publications/power-and-bipower-variation-stochastic-volatility-and-jumps ; daily-frequency heuristic, not an intraday jump estimator.

Bipower state features: append nonnegative variance-minus-bipower shares over20/60 daily returns and short/long bipower ratio to both predictors. Hypothesis distinguishing isolated moves from persistent variation adds predictive state information. Original gate and training-only tuning retained. Source Barndorff-Nielsen and Shephard (2004), https://shephard.scholars.harvard.edu/publications/power-and-bipower-variation-stochastic-volatility-and-jumps ; daily-frequency heuristic, not an intraday jump estimator.

Bipower feature normalization: scale existing momentum/trend features with adjacent-product volatility instead of standard deviation, preserving all other modeling and gate choices. Hypothesis isolated extreme returns distort ordinary volatility normalization. Source Barndorff-Nielsen and Shephard (2004), https://shephard.scholars.harvard.edu/publications/power-and-bipower-variation-stochastic-volatility-and-jumps ; daily-frequency heuristic, not an intraday jump estimator.

Moving-block bootstrap neural ensemble: fit five dropout networks to fixed-seed resamples of contiguous20-observation training blocks and average their forecasts. Choose training duration on the original purged training suffix before resampling; retain original ridge/gate. Hypothesis preserving overlapping-label dependence while resampling whole episodes reduces nonlinear estimator variance. Own adaptation; no validation fitting or seed selection.

Empirical Gaussian-rank neural targets: map monthly training returns to normal quantiles, fit the dropout network, then invert predictions through training empirical quantiles. Checkpoint selection still uses original-unit errors on the purged later training suffix. Original ridge/gate. Hypothesis rank estimation is less dominated by extreme target magnitudes; inverse mapping is a robust location heuristic rather than guaranteed conditional mean.

Hidden-direction decorrelation: add squared pairwise inner-product penalty on nonbias neural hidden weights, coefficient0.001 in the gradient, alongside original dropout and weight decay. Original ridge, clean inference, purged checkpoint choice and shock gate retained. Hypothesis discouraging redundant hidden projections preserves complementary nonlinear representations when indicators are correlated. Own regularization hypothesis.

Multiscale variance-ratio features: append log variance ratios for2/5/20-session overlapping returns against126-session daily variance to both ridge and dropout neural predictors. Hypothesis return dependence across horizons distinguishes persistent from reversing paths. Original training-only fits and gate unchanged. Inspired by Lo and MacKinlay (1988), https://web.mit.edu/~alo/www/Papers/lo-mackinlay-88.html ; descriptive rolling ratios, not significance tests.

Dependence-conditioned momentum: augment variance-ratio features with products of each log ratio and its corresponding short/monthly normalized return feature. Hypothesis explicitly conditioning momentum on serial dependence lets a shallow model express trend-versus-reversal regimes. Original ensemble/gate and purged fitting. Inspired by Lo and MacKinlay (1988), https://web.mit.edu/~alo/www/Papers/lo-mackinlay-88.html ; descriptive rolling ratios, not significance tests.

Variance-ratio regime rule: when rolling5-session variance ratio exceeds unity, follow21-session momentum; otherwise trade against5-session momentum. Use dimensionless0.1 hysteresis and original training-calibrated shock gate. Hypothesis adapting direction to observed persistence works without a fitted return predictor. Inspired by Lo and MacKinlay (1988), https://web.mit.edu/~alo/www/Papers/lo-mackinlay-88.html ; descriptive rolling ratios, not significance tests.

Execution-aware neural early stopping: select200/600/1200 training steps by simulated net log growth of the ridge-plus-dropout ensemble on the later30-percent training suffix. Fit the companion ridge and shock thresholds strictly on earlier training rows; retain21-row purge, next-open labels, drifted turnover costs and terminal liquidation. Full refit after choosing duration. Hypothesis prediction MSE can select a checkpoint with inferior trading decisions; no validation fitting.

Expanding-fold execution-aware early stopping: select neural duration by summed ensemble net log growth on three chronological20-percent training windows following40/60/80-percent prefixes. Refit ridge, dropout neural snapshots and shock calibration on each purged prefix; charge costs and liquidation separately per fold. Refit selected duration on all training data. Hypothesis averaging sequential trading outcomes is a more stable early-stopping criterion than a single MSE suffix.

Adam neural optimization: replace plain stochastic gradient updates with bias-corrected first/second gradient moments, default learning rate0.001 and beta0.9/0.999. Retain coupled weight penalty, dropout, initialization, minibatches, purged MSE checkpoint selection and ridge/gate. Hypothesis adaptive scaling fits nonlinear indicators more effectively under the fixed training budget. Kingma and Ba, submitted2014-12-22, https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.6980 .

Smoothed-gradient neural optimization: use bias-corrected exponential gradient averaging with0.9 memory while retaining original decaying learning rate and penalties. All other dropout ensemble choices unchanged. Hypothesis reducing minibatch gradient noise improves convergence without coordinate-wise adaptive scaling. Own optimizer comparison; training-only checkpoint selection.

Dropout-distribution inference: average64 fixed-seed feature-masked neural predictions per observation, with the same10-percent inverted masking used in training. Use this averaged prediction both for purged training checkpoint selection and deployment; keep ridge/gate unchanged. Hypothesis integrating nonlinear masked predictions better matches the training objective than feeding only mean inputs. Reuse identical masks for every observation; no seed search.

First-passage neural labels: replace fixed monthly targets by average forward log return up to the first cumulative move of either sign reaching twice current daily volatility, capped at20 sessions. Use only training forward returns and purge21 rows before checkpoint evaluation. Original ridge and daily reallocation/gate remain. Hypothesis early directional resolution is more predictable than a fixed calendar endpoint. Own event-label adaptation; barriers define training labels, not hindsight execution.

Variance-clock neural labels: accumulate training forward squared log returns until reaching20 times current observable daily variance, capped at60 sessions, and predict average log return over that interval. Purge61 rows for all checkpoint fitting; original ridge and actual daily execution unchanged. Hypothesis a comparable amount of market variation defines more stable prediction targets across quiet and active states. Own event-time labeling hypothesis; future observations are confined to training labels.

Robust trend replacement: substitute normalized median pairwise log-price slopes for the5/21/63-session endpoint momentum inputs, keeping all other ridge/dropout features and gate unchanged. Hypothesis using the full path reduces sensitivity to arbitrary endpoints and isolated moves. Training-only fitting retained. Trend estimator: Sen (December1968), https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.1968.10480934 .

Robust trend geometry features: append21/63-session median pairwise slopes, deviations from the fitted endpoint and pairwise directional concordance. Hypothesis trend strength, overshoot and consistency jointly distinguish continuation from reversal. Original ensemble and shock gate retained. Trend estimator: Sen (December1968), https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.1968.10480934 .

Standalone robust monthly trend: invest when the normalized21-session median pairwise log-price slope exceeds0.05, exit below-0.05, otherwise retain position; multiply by the original training-calibrated shock gate. Hypothesis a robust path trend can provide a simpler directional rule than supervised forecasts. Trend estimator: Sen (December1968), https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.1968.10480934 .

Representation ablation, robust neural only: give the dropout network median-pairwise5/21/63-session log-price slopes while preserving the original ridge endpoint-momentum representation. Keep equal forecast blend, purged training fits and gate. Hypothesis robustness helps nonlinear estimation while the linear predictor benefits from endpoint sensitivity; isolates the two components of the prior joint replacement. Sen (December1968), https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.1968.10480934 .

Representation ablation, robust ridge only: give ridge the median-pairwise momentum slopes and leave dropout neural inputs unchanged. Retain equal blend, training-only checkpoint and ridge selection, and gate. Hypothesis a smooth robust linear forecast complements the nonlinear predictor's endpoint sensitivity; reciprocal component ablation rather than a blend-weight search. Sen (December1968), https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.1968.10480934 .

Neural additive predictor: allocate four trainable tanh units to each of the nine individual features and sum their outputs, with no cross-feature hidden connections. Preserve dropout, training-only early stopping, ridge forecast blend and shock gate. Hypothesis smooth nonlinear marginal effects generalize better than unrestricted indicator interactions. Own sparse-architecture comparison; fixed connectivity, no feature or seed search.

Grouped neural predictor: allocate four tanh units to each of short returns, slow trend, and volatility/drawdown groups; permit interactions within each group but not across groups. Keep original training targets, dropout, purged checkpoint selection, ridge blend and gate. Hypothesis an intermediate structural prior captures economically related interactions while limiting unrelated combinations. Own grouped-architecture hypothesis.

State-local neural experts: partition standardized training states into four deterministic farthest-initialized k-means clusters, fit a dropout network per cluster using the globally selected training duration, and shrink the nearest expert toward the global neural prediction by n/(n+500). Original ridge and gate retained. Hypothesis differing conditional return relations across recurring states justify local nonlinear models. All clustering and labels use training only; no random seed search.

Smooth state-local neural experts: use the same four training-only k-means neural experts but average their shrunken corrections with Gaussian distance weights of bandwidth sqrt(feature_count). Original global model, ridge blend and gate unchanged. Hypothesis smooth transitions among recurring states reduce brittle nearest-cluster switches while preserving local information.

Residual two-layer neural predictor: augment the original8-unit tanh network with a4-unit tanh layer reading those hidden activations and a zero-initialized additive output head. Jointly train both paths with existing dropout/penalties and purged early stopping, preserving ridge and gate. Hypothesis compositions of learned market-state features capture effects inaccessible to a single shallow layer while retaining its direct path. Own architecture hypothesis.

Stacked two-layer neural predictor: use the same8-to4 tanh architecture but remove the direct first-layer output path, forcing predictions through the second-layer bottleneck. Retain original targets, dropout, training-only checkpoint choice, ridge blend and shock gate. Hypothesis a compact composed representation generalizes better than an unrestricted residual correction. Own structural ablation, no width or seed grid.

Fractional-memory features: append three normalized power-decay filters of trailing log returns corresponding to price differencing orders0.75/0.5/0.25, used jointly as a fixed basis. Weights use(j-d)/j recurrence and normalization by current volatility times weight norm. Hypothesis retaining smoothly decaying memory avoids abrupt lookback cutoffs. Original ensemble/gate. Inspiration: Granger and Joyeux (January1980), https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1467-9892.1980.tb00297.x ; finite causal filters only, no asserted stationarity.

Fractional-memory momentum replacement: replace endpoint5/21/63-session inputs with the fixed short-to-long fractional filter basis, preserving other features and train-only fitting. Hypothesis a smooth memory profile is a better low-dimensional summary than endpoint returns. Inspiration: Granger and Joyeux (January1980), https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1467-9892.1980.tb00297.x ; finite causal filters only, no asserted stationarity.

Standalone fractional-memory trend: average the three volatility-normalized fractional signals, enter above0.1 and exit below-0.1, retaining position between thresholds and applying the original training-calibrated shock gate. Hypothesis multi-rate long memory yields a stable directional rule without supervised fitting. Inspiration: Granger and Joyeux (January1980), https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1467-9892.1980.tb00297.x ; finite causal filters only, no asserted stationarity.

Drawdown-energy shock gate: replace short/long return volatility ratio with the ratio of5/60-session root-mean-square pullbacks from each observation's trailing20-session price high. Preserve train95/70 calibration, price confirmations and original ridge/dropout forecasts. Hypothesis persistent downside path stress is more relevant to avoiding losses than volatility from upward moves. Own causal path-risk hypothesis.

Duration-normalized drawdown gate: use log decline from the126-session high divided by trailing60 volatility times square root of sessions since that high. Preserve original train-quantile thresholds, exit confirmation, recovery logic and ensemble. Hypothesis unusually fast declines relative to their duration identify harmful states without treating all high-volatility moves alike. Own price-path hypothesis.

Drawdown geometry features: append trailing126-session maximum pullback, RMS pullback, age since high and fraction of observations more than one current daily-volatility unit underwater. Normalize magnitude features by current volatility and sqrt126. Original training-only ensemble and shock gate unchanged. Hypothesis depth, duration and persistence jointly describe market states beyond current distance to a recent high. Own feature hypothesis.

Log-volatility representation: log-transform current20-session volatility and the5/20 volatility ratio in both predictors; keep all directional features, original gate and training-only model selection unchanged. Hypothesis compressing the positive risk scale represents proportional changes more consistently across volatility regimes. Own feature-coordinate hypothesis.

Volatility term structure: append log20/60 and60/126 volatility ratios plus lag-one squared-return dependence to both predictors. Hypothesis short-lived shocks and persistent multi-horizon risk states have different conditional returns. Original training-only fit and gate retained. Horizon-component inspiration: Corsi (Spring2009), https://doi.org/10.1093/jjfinec/nbp001 ; daily close-return adaptation, not intraday HAR-RV replication.

Rolling relative-volatility context: append the current20-session volatility percentile and log ratio to its median among all20-session windows in the available252-session history. Hypothesis current risk relative to the observable recent environment transfers better than its absolute level alone. Original features, training-only fits and gate retained; no future or external distribution statistics.

Adjacent-state prediction consistency: train each minibatch on16 pairs of neighboring training observations and penalize squared differences between their dropout neural forecasts with relative coefficient0.1, alongside the original supervised errors. Pairing stays within each fitting prefix; purged checkpoint evaluation remains clean MSE. Original ridge and gate unchanged. Hypothesis monthly expected return should vary smoothly across nearby daily states, reducing unstable signal switches.

Adjacent-state change supervision: use the same paired training procedure but match predicted forecast changes to differences between the two monthly training targets instead of forcing them toward zero. Original ridge, dropout, clean purged early stopping and gate retained. Hypothesis learning changes as well as levels improves sensitivity to evolving return opportunities without shrinking every change. All difference labels remain inside training.

Factorization-machine forecast ensemble: replace tanh prediction with a linear term and rank-three pairwise feature interactions, initialized near ridge and trained with input dropout and squared loss. Select200/600/1200 steps on the same purged training suffix; retain equal ridge blend and shock gate. Hypothesis low-rank interactions share parameters more efficiently than dense quadratic features or hidden tanh units. Factorized-interaction inspiration: Rendle (ICDM2010), https://www.libfm.org/ ; independent standard-library implementation.

Standalone factorization-machine allocation: use the same training-only low-rank interaction predictor directly for the existing hysteretic long/cash decision, preserving the original shock gate. Hypothesis the model's learned linear term already supplies the ridge-like baseline and an extra equal ridge blend dilutes useful interactions. Factorized-interaction inspiration: Rendle (ICDM2010), https://www.libfm.org/ ; independent standard-library implementation.

Training-only symbolic policy discovery: evolve32 small causal expressions for10 generations using current technical features and add/subtract/multiply/negate/tanh, bounded to25 nodes and depth5. Fit on first70-percent training data with2-row purge, select generation2/5/10 champions on later training net growth, enforce training drawdown50-percent and charge trading costs. Deploy selected expression with0.05 score hysteresis and original shock gate. Hypothesis compositional rules express useful interactions missed by fixed predictors; validation used only by official runner.

Ungated symbolic policy discovery: apply the identical fixed-seed, bounded expression-fitting procedure directly to long/cash positions without the shock overlay in either training or deployment. Hypothesis a jointly learned nonlinear rule may incorporate risk information more effectively than multiplying by a fixed independent filter. All program search and checkpoint choice remain inside training; unchanged official reward and execution.
